title: Odd-frequency pair correlations in the trapped fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
authors: M. Wong, K. Thompson, M. Governale, J. Brand, U. Zuelicke
abstract: The fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas is an exactly solvable model realizing a conventional macroscopic condensate of p-wave Cooper pairs. Here we demonstrate that, when confined by a trapping potential, it also hosts unconventional odd-frequency pairing, i.e., pair correlations with s-wave symmetry that are only present with a finite time delay t between fermions forming a pair. Quantitative results for fixed particle number are obtained using a generalization of Yang's theory of off-diagonal long-range order to define a t-dependent order parameter that is antisymmetric under combined t inversion and exchange of fermion-pair indices. Odd-frequency pairing in the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas is found to be a mesoscopic effect, localized at the system's boundary and therefore nonextensive thermodynamically. Our results show that this elusive hidden order is accessible in systems having fixed particle number, suggesting new avenues towards its experimental realization and further detailed study.
summary: This theoretical study examines the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas, an exactly solvable model for strongly interacting fermions. The authors demonstrate the presence of unconventional odd-frequency pairing, which is a boundary-localized, mesoscopic phenomenon. They achieve this by generalizing ODLRO theory to analyze the time-dependent two-body correlation matrix.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and nature of unconventional odd-frequency pair correlations within the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau (FTG) gas.
main_result: Odd-frequency pairing is predicted to exist in the trapped FTG gas, but it is a mesoscopic effect localized at the system's boundary and nonextensive thermodynamically.
method: The analysis generalizes Yang's theory of Off-Diagonal Long-Range Order (ODLRO) by using the Time-Dependent Two-Body Correlation Matrix ($ho_2$) and its time-ordered counterpart ($ho_T^2$).
model_or_system: The system is the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau (FTG) gas, an exactly solvable model known to exhibit conventional p-wave Cooper pairing, which is then analyzed under the influence of a trapping potential.
key_observables: The order parameter $\phi_T^0(x, y; t)$ and the macroscopic eigenvalue $n_0(t)$ derived from the T2bCM are key diagnostics for superfluidity and pairing.
important_parameters: Fixed particle number ($N$), finite time delay ($t$), and the trapping potential $V(x)$ (harmonic or square-well).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Off-Diagonal Long-Range Approximation (ODLRO) and the use of the Time-Dependent Two-Body Correlation Matrix formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial dependence of wave functions and the time evolution of the macroscopic eigenvalue $n_0(t)$ for various particle numbers and potentials, alongside scaling plots for the odd-frequency pairing magnitude.
paper_structure: The work progresses by establishing the theoretical framework using the T2bCM, deriving the macroscopic eigenvalue $n_0(t)$ via ODLRO, and finally applying this formalism to calculate and analyze the signature of odd-frequency pairing in the trapped FTG gas.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced topics in strongly correlated quantum gases, specifically exploring unconventional pairing symmetries (odd-frequency) beyond standard BCS theory, which is highly relevant to modern AMO research.
